issues.legal_issue: A legislature cannot delegate to the executive an unguided power to decide which documents are opposed to public policy and must be refused registration.
material_facts: The law authorized the State Government to declare that registration of any document or class of documents was opposed to public policy and required registering officers to refuse registration of documents covered by such a declaration.
The law and the other provisions relied on supplied no policy or standard to guide the executive in deciding what was opposed to public policy.
Deciding whether a particular transaction is contrary to public policy requires consideration of the transaction and the case-specific material, a function the Court held belongs to the judiciary.
issues.conclusion: The provision was unconstitutional because it delegated an unguided and excessive power to the executive, contrary to Articles 14 and 246 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Delegated legislation may implement legislative policy and prescribe ancillary details, but the legislature must retain essential legislative functions and provide adequate standards to guide the delegate. An uncertain concept such as public policy, without statutory guidance, cannot itself supply those standards or transfer the judiciary’s case-specific role to the executive. The Court relied on Re: Delhi Laws Act, 1912; Rajnarain Singh v. Chairman, Patna Administration Committee; Hamdard Dawakahana v. Union of India; Kishan Prakash Sharma v. Union of India; Krishna Mohan (P) Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi; Godawat Pan Masala Products v. Union of India; and Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya, applying Articles 14 and 246 of the Constitution.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_registration_delegation and delegation_uses_undefined_public_policy and statute_provides_no_policy_or_standard and executive_decision_controls_mandatory_registration and issue_requires_judicial_case_specific_evaluation

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_registration: A party in a constitutional challenge contests a law that delegates to the executive decisions about registration of documents.
predicates.delegation_uses_undefined_public_policy: The law authorizes the executive to classify documents by whether they are opposed to public policy without defining that criterion.
predicates.statute_provides_no_policy_or_standard: The law and its relevant surrounding provisions provide no legislative policy or standard to guide the executive’s classification.
predicates.executive_decision_controls_mandatory_re: An executive classification requires registration officers to refuse documents within its scope.
predicates.issue_requires_judicial_case_specific_ev: Deciding whether the conduct or transaction is contrary to public policy requires evaluation of case-specific circumstances and material.

issues.definition: When a registration law uses an undefined public-policy criterion, provides no guiding standard, and makes the executive’s classification determine mandatory refusal despite the need for judicial case-specific evaluation, the delegated power is unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: An executive notification cannot prevent registration of an otherwise lawful power of attorney by restricting the principal’s ability to deal with property without authority in substantive law.
material_facts: A landholder executed a power of attorney authorizing an agent to manage and cultivate land and to mortgage or sell it and obtain registration of the relevant documents.

The registering officer refused to register the power of attorney under notifications that classified powers of attorney by their duration, revocability, place of presentation, or the relationship between the principal and agent.

The Court found that execution of a power of attorney was lawful and that the applicable substantive law did not make the underlying transaction illegal; the registration law dealt with documents, not the transactions embodied in them.
A person may need an agent to deal with property and cannot be prevented from dealing with that property in the absence of substantive legislation authorizing the restriction.
issues.conclusion: The notifications could not validly bar registration of the power of attorney on the stated grounds, and the refusal to register it on that basis could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: A power of attorney is an instrument of agency governed by Chapter X of the Indian Contract Act and the Power of Attorney Act, including sections 1A and 2 of the latter Act. Under sections 17, 32 and 33 of the Registration Act, registration depends on the applicable statutory requirements; the Act regulates documents rather than the transactions embodied in them. A subordinate enactment cannot restrict a lawful transaction or a person’s ability to deal with property without substantive statutory authority, consistently with Article 300A of the Constitution. The Court relied on M.E. Moolla Sons, Ltd. v. Official Assignee, Rangoon; K. Panchapagesa Ayyar v. K. Kalyanasundaram Ayyar; and Syed Abdullah Sahib v. Syed Rahmatulla Sahib.

rule.if: power_of_attorney_registration_case and power_authorizes_lawful_property_agency and no_substantive_law_prohibits_transaction and executive_notice_blocks_registration_based_on_general_category

predicates.power_of_attorney_registration_case: The proceeding concerns refusal to register an instrument appointing an agent to act for a principal.
predicates.power_authorizes_lawful_property_agency: The instrument authorizes the agent to manage, transfer, or otherwise deal with the principal’s property on the principal’s behalf.
predicates.no_substantive_law_prohibits_transaction: No substantive law makes the authorized transaction or the agency instrument illegal.
predicates.executive_notice_blocks_registration_bas: An executive notice bars registration by applying a general category to the instrument, rather than a restriction authorized by substantive law.

issues.definition: If a registration proceeding concerns a lawful property-related agency instrument and an executive notice blocks registration through a general category unsupported by substantive law, registration must not be refused on that basis.
